extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of CCR units, Participating State Directors (or EPA permitting authorities), State regulators, and other regulated stakeholders
extracted.subtask_short: CCR closure and corrective action compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for closing Coal Combustion Residual (CCR) units under a new closure alternative while complying with groundwater monitoring and corrective action obligations, including document retention, deed notation, certification, and timing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and concurrency of closure and corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing regulations, the closure requirements and the corrective action requirements operate independent of one another, and facilities are required to comply with both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA rejects the claim that closure must be completed prior to initiating corrective action; closure and corrective action obligations run concurrently and cannot be delayed in favor of the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACM initiation and completion deadlines (§257.96(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACM must be initiated within 90 days of determining an SSL has occurred, and then completed within another 90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An extension not to exceed 60 days may be warranted due to site-specific conditions or circumstances. EPA did not revise these deadlines in this rulemaking; suggestions to change them are outside scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy selection timing and public involvement (§257.97(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the ACM is complete, a public meeting has been held, and community input has been considered, a remedy must be selected as soon as feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected groundwater remediation must be implemented within a reasonable time in accordance with the schedule established in the remedy selection report; implementation of source control alone does not satisfy the separate groundwater remediation requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source control does not satisfy groundwater remediation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation of the source control measure does not satisfy the separate requirement to implement the groundwater remediation portion of the remedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if closure by removal is used to satisfy source control, the groundwater remediation portion must still be implemented per the remedy schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACM content: attenuation mechanisms and site characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: The ACM must include identification of attenuation mechanisms and characterization of site conditions influencing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This characterization can be based on current site conditions and modeled future conditions and can rely on data and knowledge facilities already possess (e.g., groundwater flow, geology, wastestreams).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitored Natural Attenuation (MNA) feasibility and monitoring needs
rubrics_metrics.description: MNA may be selected if evaluated favorably but requires monitoring (installation of additional downgradient wells) rather than construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MNA does not require delay due to closure activities; installation of downgradient wells should not be affected by unit closure. However, MNA will not meet §257.97(b) unless there is evidence that permanent immobilization mechanisms are viable under current or modeled future conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely completion of remedial activities (§257.98(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedial activities must be completed within a reasonable period; delaying remedy implementation until after closure would be inconsistent with §257.98(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collecting monitoring data is the primary action for many remedies (e.g., MNA); delaying monitoring loses critical data and is therefore contrary to timely implementation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring must not be delayed during closure
rubrics_metrics.description: Groundwater monitoring (data collection) necessary for corrective action must occur during closure and cannot reasonably be postponed until after closure is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delayed data collection results in lost opportunities to evaluate remedies; monitoring during closure is required to proceed with corrective action as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptive remedy requirement (§257.98(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after the remedy is implemented, it is determined that compliance is not being achieved, the owner or operator is required to 'implement other methods or techniques that could feasibly achieve compliance'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional measures can be undertaken after certification of closure without impacting the facility's closure certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for the closure alternative requires initiation of remedial activities (§257.98(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner or operator must have initiated the remedial activities as required by §257.98(a) in order to be eligible for this closure alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sole exception: if corrective action was triggered so late in the closure process that it was not feasible to delay closure until a remedy could be selected. In that case, the facility must document (1) compliance with §§257.96–257.98 and (2) that it could not extend the active life of the unit consistent with §257.102(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-closure care duration tied to corrective action completion (§257.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: For units closed under this provision, the CCR unit remains subject to post-closure care until groundwater corrective action has been completed; not automatically for 30 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA clarified that post-closure care ends under §257.104(c) after 30 years unless the unit remains in assessment monitoring; to conclude post-closure care, the owner/operator must return to detection monitoring (no detections of any Appendix IV constituents for two consecutive sampling events).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to conduct groundwater monitoring and corrective action (§§257.90–257.98)
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner or operator must conduct groundwater monitoring and corrective action in accordance with the requirements of §§257.90 through 257.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule does not change the existing groundwater monitoring and corrective action program requirements; those procedures remain in force for units closed under the alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure plan revision and post-closure care plan preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators closing under this new closure alternative must revise their written closure plan and prepare an initial post-closure care plan within six months of the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The closure plan describes the closure and schedule; post-closure care plan describes maintenance after closure. Existing procedures for amending plans (e.g., §257.102(b)(3)(ii)) apply. EPA considers six months (or one year from publication) reasonable because facility should already have prepared closure plans and begun corrective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deed notation requirement until groundwater corrective action completion (§257.102(i)(4) and §257.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must record a notation on the deed (or other instrument normally examined during title search) notifying potential purchasers that the land has been used as a CCR unit and is subject to ongoing groundwater corrective action requirements until corrective action is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deed notation ensures future owners are on notice of ongoing cleanup obligations and potential liability. To remove the deed notation (or add a second notation reflecting inapplicability), the owner/operator must (1) demonstrate monitoring concentrations no longer exceed groundwater protection standards established pursuant to §257.95(h) for Appendix IV constituents (§257.104(g)), and (2) complete the notification stating post-closure care requirements have been met (§257.104(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deed notation alternatives considered but rejected
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA considered allowing other legal instruments (e.g., Environmental Use Restrictions/Environmental Covenants) or state discretion, but concluded none provided sufficient assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalized recordation of a deed notation because commenters did not provide sufficient information that alternatives would provide the same level of notice and liability assurance; also aligns with MSW landfill requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure certification or approval requirement (§257.102(f)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must obtain a certification from a qualified P.E. or approval from the Participating State Director (or EPA where EPA is permitting authority) verifying that closure has been completed in accordance with the written closure plan and all applicable closure requirements of §257.102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification/approval indicates that all removal and decontamination activities, except groundwater corrective action, have been completed; it does not address remediation of impacted groundwater (which continues during post-closure care).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition clarification: 'technically feasible/feasible' and 'technically infeasible/infeasible'
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA clarified that 'technically feasible' and 'feasible' have the same meaning, and that 'technically infeasible' and 'infeasible' have the same meaning in the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definitions read: 'Technically feasible or feasible means possible to do in a way that would likely be successful.' EPA finalized these synonymous definitions and codified in §257.53.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wetlands CFR reference correction (§257.61(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct the CFR reference for the wetlands definition in §257.61(a) to 40 CFR 230.41(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA reviewed impacts of Sackett v. EPA and determined the wetlands definition in §257.61(a) remains valid; the amendment updates an incorrect cross-reference introduced by prior rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater monitoring and corrective action applicability correction (§257.90(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct typographical error referring to the scope of groundwater monitoring and corrective action requirements to refer to §§257.90 through 257.98 (not §257.99).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change avoids confusion and aligns section references with codified requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCR website terminology and combined-website flexibility (§257.107(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize term to 'CCR website' and allow the owner/operator to maintain one website for multiple electric power sector rules provided postings are delineated under separate headings for each regulatory program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: place CCR postings under 'CCR Rule Compliance Data and Information' and ELG postings under 'ELG Rule Compliance Data and Information'. This flexibility aims to reduce paperwork burden and improve public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document retention and posting periods tied to relevance and unit status
rubrics_metrics.description: Retention times for documents in the facility operating record and on the facility CCR website are extended and tied to the nature of each document and its relevance to operation, closure, and cleanup; for many documents EPA chose five years as the reasonable posting/retention period after milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA adopted an approach used in the 2015 Rule (retain until remedy completion for some documents) and will require longer retention where relevance persists. The approach links retention/posting to unit status and milestones, and allows longer retention in operating record than on website for some documents to avoid clutter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprovisioning of previously removed or destroyed required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents that may have been taken down or removed from operating records but are still relevant must be placed back in the operating records and reposted on the website; if destroyed or discarded, they must be reproduced and reposted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents inconsistencies among facility websites and ensures information relevant to each CCR unit remains publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity on which versions of documents to post
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple versions of a document exist (e.g., periodic assessments or updates), the regulations specify what version(s) must be posted and retained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from Table 3: some items require 'retain all' in operating record but only current or current plus previous one on website; others require retention until closure is complete or until post-closure care is complete. EPA is revising regulations to clarify these versioning requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific document retention rules (Table 3 examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 3 lists specific retention/posting requirements for named documents (location restrictions demonstration; landfill liner and leachate collection certifications; documentation of liner type; surface impoundment liner certifications; permanent identification marker documentation; initial and periodic hazard potential classification assessments; emergency action plan and revisions; records of annual face-to-face meetings with local responders; records of emergency action plan activations; history of construction; initial and periodic structural stability assessments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: many documents are to be retained in the operating record and posted on the CCR website for 5 years after closure by removal (CBR) or after post-closure care ends; some are to be retained until closure is complete (not including meeting GWPS) for CBR or until post-closure care is complete for closure in place (CIP); some items require 'retain all' versions in the operating record.
